brief.paper_summary:
由于现实世界中的大多数数据都可以用图表示，因此近年来针对图表示学
习的研究越来越受到关注。通过将高维图数据转化成低维的表征向量，图表示
学习可以有效地对图的信息进行存储并快捷地访问图中实体的关键知识。利用
学习到的图表征数据可以为社交网络行为分析、节点分类、链路预测和聚类等
下游任务提供帮助。随着深度学习的快速发展，研究人员提出了基于图神经网
络的图表示学习方法，其使图中的节点能够同时学习图的结构信息以及邻域节
点的特征信息，从而得到高质量的低维表征。针对图神经网络上的图表示学
习，本文主要关注两个问题：大规模时序图场景下的图表示学习方法和分布式
场景下的大规模图的图神经网络优化训练方法。
真实世界中的图数据规模往往十分庞大且处于动态变化的状态，而现有的
图神经网络要么无法处理动态时序图上的图表征学习，要么面对大规模图数据
集时训练效率低下。为了解决大规模动态图上的图表征学习问题，本文提出了
一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法——GSAERU 模型。GSAERU 模
型由“图表征学习模块”和“时序学习模块”两部分构成。首先将动态时序图
建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列，接着在单时间步上将图快照输入图表征学习
模块。该模块通过图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，并将压缩后的新图输入图自编
码器，利用和原图的重构误差训练原图节点的表征。在获得单时间步上的图表
征后将其输入时序学习模块，并通过一个循环神经网络学习原图在时间维度上
的特征信息与依赖关系，从而得到大规模时序图的高质量表征。基于在四个真
实世界的大规模图数据集上的大量实验表明，GSAERU 模型能够高效生成时序
图的表征。与传统的图神经网络算法相比，其平均内存消耗和平均训练时长只
有其9.86% 与13.27%，且与性能最好的算法在大部分指标下的差距都不超过
3.5%。

ii
使用分布式技术加速神经网络训练也是如今热门的研究课题，因为在处理
大规模数据时，单个设备（如CPU，GPU）有限的内存和计算资源往往会成为
训练瓶颈。而分布式技术可以提供更多的计算资源来提高训练效率。然而由于
图数据的不规则性，传统分布式机器学习方法中的子任务划分和模型训练方法
难以直接应用于图神经网络。针对大规模图流数据场景下的分布式图神经网络
训练优化问题，本文提出了基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络优化训练算法——
DSGNN 模型。DSGNN 模型采用“领导——工作者”工作模式，首先由领导节
点利用一个基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分并将划分子图分配给各
个工作节点。工作节点随后执行一个基于图摘要技术的小批量训练并将训练结
果通过一个注意力层返回给领导节点，最后由领导节点汇总结果并计算梯度，
并根据梯度同步更新所有计算节点上的模型。基于四个真实世界的大规模图数
据集上的大量实验，结果表明DSGNN 模型可以大大加速GNN 模型的训练，
并且在链路预测任务上的F1 分数显著高于其它分布式图神经网络模型。
brief.research_problem: 面向大规模动态图的图神经网络优化机制研究

novelty_points.claim: 提出一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法GSAERU，通过图摘要技术将动态时序图压缩为固定规模的新图，解决GNN输出无法直接输入RNN的问题，并利用图自编码器与循环神经网络学习时序特征。
novelty_points.claim_en: Propose a large-scale sequential graph representation learning method GSAERU based on graph summarization, which compresses dynamic sequential graphs into fixed-size new graphs via graph summarization to solve the problem that GNN outputs cannot be directly fed into RNN, and uses graph autoencoder and recurrent neural network to learn temporal features.
technical_features: 将动态时序图建模为各时刻原图快照的序列
在单时间步上利用图摘要技术压缩原图，将压缩后的新图输入图自编码器，通过重构误差训练原图节点表征
将单时间步图表征输入循环神经网络，学习时间维度上的特征信息与依赖关系
technical_features_en: Model dynamic sequential graphs as a sequence of snapshots of the original graph at each time step

Compress the original graph via graph summarization at a single time step, input the compressed new graph into a graph autoencoder, and train node representations using reconstruction error with the original graph
Feed the single-time-step graph representations into a recurrent neural network to learn temporal features and dependencies
source_locations: 摘要：GSAERU 模型由“图表征学习模块”和“时序学习模块”两部分构成。首先将动态时序图建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列，接着在单时间步上将图快照输入图表征学习模块。该模块通过图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，并将压缩后的新图输入图自编码器，利用和原图的重构误差训练原图节点的表征。在获得单时间步上的图表征后将其输入时序学习模块，并通过一个循环神经网络学习原图在时间维度上的特征信息与依赖关系
作者贡献段1：GSAERU 模型通过引入图摘要技术将原图映射到固定规模的新图中，解决了GNN 模型输出无法直接输入到RNN 模型中进行训练的问题

novelty_points.claim: 提出一种基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络训练框架DSGNN，采用“领导-工作者”模式，领导节点负责图划分和模型同步更新，工作节点基于图摘要技术进行小批量训练，并通过注意力层返回结果。
novelty_points.claim_en: Propose a distributed graph neural network training framework DSGNN based on graph summarization, adopting a leader-worker mode where the leader node performs graph partitioning and synchronous model updates, and worker nodes conduct mini-batch training based on graph summarization and return results via an attention layer.
technical_features: 采用“领导-工作者”工作模式
领导节点利用基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分并分配子图
工作节点执行基于图摘要技术的小批量训练
训练结果通过注意力层返回给领导节点
领导节点汇总结果并计算梯度，同步更新所有计算节点上的模型
technical_features_en: The leader node partitions the original graph using an edge-segmentation-based graph stream partitioning algorithm and assigns subgraphs
Workers perform mini-batch training based on graph summarization
Training results are returned to the leader through an attention layer
The leader aggregates results, computes gradients, and synchronously updates models on all computing nodes
source_locations: 摘要：DSGNN 模型采用“领导——工作者”工作模式，首先由领导节点利用一个基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分并将划分子图分配给各个工作节点。工作节点随后执行一个基于图摘要技术的小批量训练并将训练结果通过一个注意力层返回给领导节点，最后由领导节点汇总结果并计算梯度，并根据梯度同步更新所有计算节点上的模型
作者贡献段2：提出了一种新的基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络训练框架，称为DSGNN，用于分布式场景下的基于图神经网络的图表示学习。与现有的独立采样分布式图神经网络训练框架不同，该模型可以在工作节点上对子图进行小批量样本的学习，而不是让领导节点完成子图生成

novelty_points.claim: 提出一种基于边分割的图流划分算法Sketch-DBH，利用Count-Min Sketch存储节点度数信息，并使用最小堆维护高频节点信息，实现常数时间内返回查询结果并生成子图编号，确保负载均衡。
novelty_points.claim_en: Propose an edge-segmentation-based graph stream partitioning algorithm Sketch-DBH, which uses Count-Min Sketch to store node degree information and a min-heap to maintain high-frequency node information, enabling constant-time query results and generating subgraph IDs to ensure load balancing.
technical_features: 使用Count-Min Sketch概率数据结构存储每个节点的度数信息
使用最小堆维护图流数据中的高频节点信息
在常数时间内返回查询结果
根据节点度数信息生成单条图流数据即将被分配到的子图编号
高效完成大规模图流数据的划分且确保负载均衡
technical_features_en: Use Count-Min Sketch probabilistic data structure to store degree information of each node
Use a min-heap to maintain high-frequency node information in graph stream data
Return query results in constant time
Generate the subgraph ID to which a single graph stream data item will be assigned based on node degree information
Efficiently partition large-scale graph stream data and ensure load balancing
source_locations: 作者贡献段2：提出了一种新的基于边分割的图流划分算法——Sketch-DBH，用于处理大规模图流数据下的子图划分问题。该算法通过Count-Min Sketch 这一概率数据结构存储每个节点的度数信息，并使用一个最小堆维护图流数据中的高频节点信息，使其可以在常数时间内返回查询结果并以此根据节点度数信息生成单条图流数据即将被分配到的子图编号。Sketch-DBH 算法可以高效完成大规模图流数据的划分且确保负载均衡

evidence_cards.document_title: Learning Dual Dynamic Representations on Time-Sliced User-Item Interaction Graphs for Sequential Recommendation
evidence_cards.main_contribution: DRL-SRe models dynamic user-item interaction graphs as time-sliced snapshots and learns user/item representations via time-sliced graph neural networks, with an auxiliary temporal prediction task based on temporal point process for sequential recommendation.
overlaps: Models dynamic sequential graphs as a sequence of per-time-slice snapshots of the interaction graph (overlaps technical feature 1 of GSAERU).
Learns graph-based representations over consecutive time slices to capture temporal dynamics.
differences: DRL-SRe does not use graph summarization to compress the original graph into a fixed-size new graph; it directly builds a global user-item interaction graph for each time slice.
DRL-SRe does not employ a graph autoencoder trained via reconstruction error against the original graph; it uses time-sliced graph neural networks.
DRL-SRe captures temporal dependencies via a temporal point process auxiliary task rather than feeding single-time-step graph representations into a recurrent neural network (RNN).
DRL-SRe targets sequential recommendation, whereas GSAERU targets large-scale sequential graph representation learning.

sources.title: Learning Dual Dynamic Representations on Time-Sliced User-Item Interaction Graphs for Sequential Recommendation
sources.quote: the proposed model builds a global user-item interaction graph for each time slice and exploits time-sliced graph neural networks to learn user and item representations

evidence_cards.document_title: ABC: Aggregation before Communication, a Communication Reduction Framework for Distributed Graph Neural Network Training and Effective Partition
evidence_cards.main_contribution: ABC proposes a lossless communication reduction method (Aggregation before Communication) for distributed GNN training, exploiting the permutation-invariant property of GNN layers and introducing a vertex-cut partition paradigm.
overlaps: Addresses distributed GNN training with graph partitioning across machines
Focuses on reducing communication in distributed GNN training
differences: Focuses on communication reduction via aggregation-before-communication and vertex-cut partitioning, not graph summarization
Does not mention a leader-worker mode with a leader node performing partitioning and synchronous model updates
Does not mention returning training results via an attention layer

sources.title: ABC: Aggregation before Communication, a Communication Reduction Framework for Distributed Graph Neural Network Training and Effective Partition
sources.quote: we study the communication complexity during distributed GNNs training and propose a simple lossless communication reduction method, termed the Aggregation before Communication (ABC) method.

sources.title: ABC: Aggregation before Communication, a Communication Reduction Framework for Distributed Graph Neural Network Training and Effective Partition
sources.quote: ABC method exploits the permutation-invariant property of the GNNs layer and leads to a paradigm where vertex-cut is proved to admit a superior communication performance than the currently popular paradigm (edge-cut).

evidence_cards.document_title: SDT-GNN: Streaming-based Distributed Training Framework for Graph Neural Networks
evidence_cards.main_contribution: SDT-GNN proposes a streaming-based distributed GNN training framework that takes a stream of edges as input for graph partitioning (SPRING algorithm) to reduce memory requirements, enabling distributed GNN training on large graphs.
overlaps: Proposes a distributed GNN training framework (similar to DSGNN's overall objective)
Performs graph partitioning to distribute workload across machines
differences: Uses streaming edge-based graph partitioning (SPRING) rather than graph summarization for mini-batch training
Does not mention a leader-worker mode with a leader node performing partitioning and synchronous model updates
Does not mention returning training results via an attention layer

sources.title: SDT-GNN: Streaming-based Distributed Training Framework for Graph Neural Networks
sources.quote: we propose SDT-GNN, a streaming-based distributed GNN training framework. Unlike the existing frameworks that load the entire graph in memory, it takes a stream of edges as input for graph partitioning to reduce the memory requirement for partitioning.

sources.title: SDT-GNN: Streaming-based Distributed Training Framework for Graph Neural Networks
sources.quote: to improve the quality of partitioning, we propose SPRING, a novel streaming partitioning algorithm for distributed GNN training.

evidence_cards.document_title: 2PS: High-Quality Edge Partitioning with Two-Phase Streaming
evidence_cards.main_contribution: Proposes 2PS, a two-phase streaming edge partitioning algorithm that separates vertices into clusters in the first phase and performs edge partitioning in the second phase, achieving low replication factor with low memory overhead.
overlaps: Streaming assignment of edges to partitions
Load balancing and replication minimization objectives
differences: Uses a two-phase streaming clustering approach rather than edge-segmentation with Count-Min Sketch
Does not use Count-Min Sketch probabilistic data structure for degree storage
Does not use a min-heap to maintain high-frequency node information
No constant-time query mechanism for subgraph ID generation is described

sources.title: 2PS: High-Quality Edge Partitioning with Two-Phase Streaming
sources.quote: In this paper, we propose 2PS, a novel two-phase streaming algorithm for high-quality edge partitioning. In the first phase, vertices are separated into clusters by a lightweight streaming clustering algorithm. In the second phase, the graph is re-streamed and edge partitioning is performed while taking into account the clustering of the vertices from the first phase.

evidence_cards.main_contribution: Proposes WStream, a window-based streaming graph partitioning algorithm (edge-cut partitioning) that partitions large graph data while keeping load balanced across partitions and minimizing communication.
overlaps: Graph stream partitioning method domain (streaming one-pass graph partitioning)
Load balancing across partitions as a core objective
Assigning graph data items to partitions/subgraphs
differences: Uses a window-based edge-cut partitioning strategy rather than edge-segmentation with Count-Min Sketch
Does not use Count-Min Sketch probabilistic data structure for degree storage
Does not use a min-heap to maintain high-frequency node information
No constant-time query mechanism for subgraph ID generation is described

sources.title: Window-based Streaming Graph Partitioning Algorithm
sources.quote: This paper proposes an efficient window-based streaming graph partitioning algorithm called WStream. The WStream algorithm is an edge-cut partitioning algorithm, which distributes a vertex among the partitions. Our results suggest that the WStream algorithm is able to partition large graph data efficiently while keeping the load balanced across different partitions, and communication to a minimum.
